result.keywords: We study a locally differentially private frequency estimation problem in which a server must recover the most frequent items from a large domain while preserving user privacy. We propose a new randomized sketching algorithm that achieves near-optimal error as a function of the domain size, the privacy budget, and the failure probability. Our approach combines compressed representations of user reports with a refined decoding procedure that improves upon standard count-sketch style baselines. We also establish lower bounds showing that the dependence on the failure probability is unavoidable in the local model. In addition, we derive a transformation that converts a broad class of interactive local protocols into simpler non-interactive mechanisms with only a modest loss in accuracy. These results have applications to histogram release, frequency moments, and robust data analytics under privacy constraints.
result.title: Adaptive Sketching for Private Frequency Estimation.
